title: Vandalizer RA usability — implementation reassessment
status: Heuristic reassessment complete; eight execution and observation checks remain
deployment: Local uncommitted working tree; not deployed

rubric.ui: Hierarchy, readability, spacing, visual consistency and responsive layout.
rubric.ux: Discoverability, keyboard access, scope retention, recovery and completion paths.
rubric.ra: Observable fit for research-administration tasks, evidence inspection, reuse and handoff. Not measured AI accuracy or demonstrated time savings.
rubric.scale: 9 exceptional; 8 strong with small friction; 7 useful with noticeable friction; 6 substantial learning or accessibility cost; 5 a serious limitation on the tested surface. Half-point grades are reviewer judgments, not precision measurements.

method: Separate heuristic reassessment of every area and viewport using the original rubric, by the same implementation agent (not an independent human reviewer). Scores describe sampled interface/task fit, not model accuracy, accessibility certification, user-study success or measured time savings. No overall average is used.

surfaces.scoreReason: Persistent labels and pane controls preserve document-to-Library composition. Five-width navigation and scope-return checks pass.
surfaces.remainingFriction: The 320px rail consumes useful horizontal space, but actions remain named and reachable.

surfaces.scoreReason: The entry gives an RA task starting point; real password/reset/invitation failures retain input and offer recovery.
surfaces.remainingFriction: External SSO is not configured in the isolated environment.

surfaces.scoreReason: Optional task actions, a labeled sample result and its linked evidence let a new RA begin before taking a course. Tour dismissal and return persist.
surfaces.remainingFriction: The compact layout needs scrolling to see the full example.

surfaces.scoreReason: Source identity, approximate page labels, missing-source recovery, bounded scope controls and retained draft/reading position support checking an answer.
surfaces.remainingFriction: Actual model grounding remains unverified; the grade covers the interaction and evidence-checking design.

surfaces.scoreReason: The proposed action, inputs and result are reviewable; pending, cancellation, failure and completion remain distinct. History does not imply an unrelated later action succeeded.
surfaces.remainingFriction: Actual model-driven approval/cancellation effects remain an execution gate.

surfaces.scoreReason: PDF, scan, DOCX and XLSX cases preserve viewing, search and recovery. File-to-Library selection survives tool runs and return. Actual project PDF read/download permissions pass.
surfaces.remainingFriction: An image-only scan needs readable extraction before grounded use; the interface explains that limit.

surfaces.scoreReason: Project intent, pinned tools, role-aware management and independent drafts are explicit. Real owner/editor/viewer, invitation and removal checks pass.
surfaces.remainingFriction: Dense projects require filtering; the compact view exposes fewer records at once.

surfaces.scoreReason: Task search, scope guidance, saved references versus copies, and failure recovery make reusable tools easier to find and maintain.
surfaces.remainingFriction: Type and scope filters still require familiarity with the tool catalog.

surfaces.scoreReason: Task/input/output descriptions and measured evidence precede adoption; the saved-reference/copy distinction is visible and failed adoption retains the selection.
surfaces.remainingFriction: Some shared tools have incomplete author-supplied examples; missing evidence is disclosed.

surfaces.scoreReason: Named step/task controls, input readiness, visible step roles and a usable output/history/save path support repeatable RA reviews. The real approval-to-export task path passes.
surfaces.remainingFriction: The design surface remains an advanced task and takes more scrolling on a phone.

surfaces.scoreReason: Results identify the current source; Inspect and Copy are separate. Missing/unconfirmed values, document switching and export limitations remain visible.
surfaces.remainingFriction: Actual extraction/model-answer correctness still needs a configured model.

surfaces.scoreReason: Setup summarizes trigger, source, action and destination; persisted outcomes distinguish queued, failed and completed runs. Actual manual/folder/schedule task paths deliver files and avoid repeated-event execution.
surfaces.remainingFriction: The execution exercise invokes task bodies locally; no distributed broker consumer or external receiver was tested.

surfaces.scoreReason: Readability, indexed source status, provenance and failure recovery are distinct from answer quality. Retrying a source preserves previously usable content and scope.
surfaces.remainingFriction: Indexed text can be available without permission to download the original; this is now explained.

surfaces.scoreReason: Named expected answers, per-case failures, sample-size limits and separate advanced tuning make measured evidence interpretable.
surfaces.remainingFriction: Model-backed workflow/KB/extraction validation is still an open execution gate.

surfaces.scoreReason: Keyboard-openable events show durable outcome/error text. Open/Delete are separate; completed and failed runs return to their actual result rather than an old approval.
surfaces.remainingFriction: A long activity feed remains dense, with filtering and scrolling necessary.

surfaces.scoreReason: Instructions, original source, editable artifact and decision consequences are clear. Real concurrent decisions accept one winner and resume/export the exact reviewed artifact.
surfaces.remainingFriction: An approval records a decision; downstream completion is checked separately.

surfaces.scoreReason: Account access and team roles are distinguished. Pending writes, invitation identity, ownership transfer, removal and password/session persistence are verified.
surfaces.remainingFriction: Institutional identity-provider administration remains outside this local test.

surfaces.scoreReason: Role guidance, masked secrets, connection-test recovery and deletion impact make maintenance understandable without asking ordinary RAs to manage secrets.
surfaces.remainingFriction: External service connectivity was simulated; the dependent-run failure was fixture-driven.

surfaces.scoreReason: Subject/problem entry comes first. Failed messages and attachments survive close/reopen and can be retried without losing the draft.
surfaces.remainingFriction: Actual ticket delivery and staff handling were simulated, with no messages sent to real people.

surfaces.scoreReason: An optional short RA walkthrough precedes the course. Actual first-module progress, interruption/resumption, saved reflection, completion and Foundations unlock pass; completion has keyboard focus and readable status.
surfaces.remainingFriction: The full course and model-backed labs remain unverified. No learning outcome or time-saving claim is inferred.

surfaces.scoreReason: A proposal/source-checking quickstart, recovery examples and contextual links lead into the technical reference. Narrow layouts preserve text and keyboard-scrollable examples.
surfaces.remainingFriction: Long-form reference sections still require reading and navigation.

surfaces.scoreReason: Responsive sections, bounded tables, readable comparisons and explicit metric limits support investigating usage and failed work without implying compliance.
surfaces.remainingFriction: Operational usefulness still needs observation by a real team owner.

surfaces.scoreReason: Candidates expose regressions and uncertainty before Apply. Failed actions can recover; real repeated Apply and stale Revert tests preserve the correct configuration history.
surfaces.remainingFriction: Candidate scores were seeded; this does not establish optimization quality.

surfaces.scoreReason: Readiness evidence, claim ownership, retained workshop edits and required decision notes support review; authors can see feedback without examiner permissions.
surfaces.remainingFriction: A real examiner observation and model-backed evidence review remain open.

surfaces.scoreReason: Responsive triage, keyboard entry, retained drafts/files, watcher recovery and explicit internal-note visibility support case handling. The mobile reply now uses the full row.
surfaces.remainingFriction: Long ticket threads need scrolling; actual staff observation remains open.

limits: Actual screen-reader use, five-RA acceptance study and specialist observations have not occurred.
Real chat grounding, agent actions, model-backed validation and the full learning course need a configured development model connection.
Most browser evidence uses explicit synthetic API fixtures. Live local backend evidence is separately identified and uses synthetic accounts/data.
Actual local task bodies were exercised with isolated Mongo/Redis and file/SMTP sinks; no production data, broker consumer or external-service delivery was used.

verification.Frontend: 1,267 tests / 198 files passed. Typecheck and production build passed. Full lint: zero errors, 14 warnings; final changed-component lint: zero errors, one existing hook-dependency warning.
verification.Final browser checks: 30 five-width file-to-Library states; 33 chat/source states including delayed initial scope; 42 actual 200% Chrome zoom states; 14 staff recovery states; nine actual local public-entry/first-module learning states. Earlier five-width 105 and enlarged-text 42 scans are indexed separately.
verification.Backend: Actual isolated auth, team/project permissions, PDF storage/text extraction, atomic review/resume/export, workflow tuning persistence and manual/folder/schedule automation checks are separately recorded. Focused regression batches are listed in the implementation log; no model inference or external receiver success is inferred.
verification.New findings closed: Duplicate invitation misuse, project-file role gaps, duplicate review decisions, repeated Apply/stale Revert, repeated automation events, mobile source/reply space, learning modal contrast/focus, initial draft-scope loss and citation-return races.
verification.Remaining sessions: The acceptance guide and three fictional sources with 12 manually checked questions are ready. Actual screen-reader, model-backed labs/grounding and RA/specialist observations remain open.

openItems: R8-BASE-07 · P1 · Verify: Audit keyboard and assistive technology paths.

Exercise row opening, card editing, menus, tabs, source links and recovery with the keyboard, then spot-check names, order and announcements with a screen reader. Automated scans do not close this item by themselves.
R8-CHAT-02 · P2 · Verify: Check grounding and evidence navigation.

Use a manually checked set of sponsor/policy questions, including missing or conflicting information. Check deadline and budget claims against the cited passages; source inspection must preserve the conversation and reading position.
R8-AGENT-03 · P2 · Verify: Exercise actual tool lifecycle transitions.

In isolated test execution, cover approval, cancellation, permission denial, interrupted streaming and retry. Confirm one accepted action produces one intended effect, including when the user refreshes or resends.
R8-VALIDATE-04 · P2 · Verify: Cover all three validation domains.

Test KB, workflow and extraction validation with real-shaped cases, missing references, cancellation, refresh/resumption, history and apply/revert. Manually compare selected results with expected answers; fixture scores alone cannot close this item.
R8-LEARN-03 · P2 · Verify: Complete a representative learning path.

Exercise lesson progress, assessment feedback, interruption/resumption, module unlock and course completion states. Check keyboard, mobile, short viewports and saved progress using controlled test accounts.
R8-GATE-03 · P2 · Verify: Check real execution separately from fixtures.

Run representative flows against an isolated backend and controlled accounts, with non-delivering external-service stubs where needed. Record ingestion, persistence, worker/retry behavior, permission enforcement and model-answer spot checks separately from visual evidence.
R8-GATE-04 · P2 · Verify: Validate RA usefulness with representative users.

Use a proposed acceptance study of at least five representative RAs performing five tasks: find a deadline, check a budget requirement, verify an extracted value, run a reusable review, and hand off a result. At least four of five users should complete each task unaided, with no unnoticed wrong-source or unintended-approval error. Record time, errors, evidence checks and handoff usability; this is a formative gate, not a statistical guarantee.
R8-GATE-05 · P2 · Verify: Validate specialist task fit with the right roles.

Observe a team owner investigating a failed run, an integration maintainer repairing a connection, an examiner reviewing a submission and support staff responding to a ticket. Ordinary RAs must also be able to identify when they need these roles and where to request help.
